PullRequest.Title: Drop pending system notifications when the user stops a chat request
PullRequest.Body:

## Problem

In the local agent chat, when a background terminal command finishes while the agent is still working, its "`<command>` completed" **System notification** waits in the pending list until the turn ends. If you stop the request at that point (Stop button or Alt+Backspace), that notification stays pending for good. The next message you send is not sent. Instead, chat asks "You already have pending requests. Do you want to keep them in the queue or remove them before sending this message?", about a message you never wrote. If you choose **Keep Pending Requests**, your message is sent and then the old notification is sent too, which starts a new agent turn about the work you just stopped. On Windows and macOS this prompt is a native dialog by default. Tools that only capture the window contents don't show it, so there the chat just looks stuck.

## Root cause

- `run_in_terminal` queues each background-command completion as a system-initiated steering request ([runInTerminalTool.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0861b77b3fe8d0d4e2b47c121ef0d2b68fa35992/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/tools/runInTerminalTool.ts#L3222-L3228)).
- When a request ends, `ChatService` sends the queue only if the request was not cancelled ([chatServiceImpl.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0861b77b3fe8d0d4e2b47c121ef0d2b68fa35992/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatService/chatServiceImpl.ts#L2267-L2269), [L2315-L2317](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0861b77b3fe8d0d4e2b47c121ef0d2b68fa35992/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatService/chatServiceImpl.ts#L2315-L2317)). After a stop, queued messages wait, and the next send asks whether to keep them ([chatWidget.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0861b77b3fe8d0d4e2b47c121ef0d2b68fa35992/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatWidget.ts#L4000-L4002), [L4321-L4359](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0861b77b3fe8d0d4e2b47c121ef0d2b68fa35992/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatWidget.ts#L4321-L4359)). That is intended for messages the user wrote.
- `run_in_terminal` already drops notifications that arrive after the user stopped the agent ([runInTerminalTool.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0861b77b3fe8d0d4e2b47c121ef0d2b68fa35992/src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/browser/tools/runInTerminalTool.ts#L3063-L3086), added in #309611). But nothing removes a notification that was queued before the stop: `cancelCurrentRequestForSession` cancels the request and leaves the queue as it is ([chatServiceImpl.ts](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/blob/0861b77b3fe8d0d4e2b47c121ef0d2b68fa35992/src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatService/chatServiceImpl.ts#L2637-L2672)). So the notification stays pending until a later turn completes, and meanwhile it triggers the prompt above.

## Fix

When a request is stopped through `cancelCurrentRequestForSession`, `ChatService` now also removes the system-initiated requests waiting in the session's local queue. This matches what `run_in_terminal` does for notifications that arrive after the stop. Removed requests are rejected the same way as any other pending request that is removed.

Deliberately unchanged:
- Messages the user queued or used to steer stay in the queue after a stop, as before.
- **Send now** on a queued message (`sendPendingRequestImmediately`) also cancels the running request, but the agent keeps working there. It uses a private variant of the cancel that keeps queued notifications, so they still follow the message.
- Agent Host sessions, whose queue is managed by the host, are not touched.

## Before / after

Both recordings run the same scenario on a dev build with a small test extension (below). It adds an `@repro` participant and an offline model, so no Copilot sign-in is needed. The participant starts a background command that prints 12 lines after 5 seconds, and then keeps working for about 15 seconds. The scenario waits until the command's System notification is pending, stops the request with Alt+Backspace, and sends `@repro hello after stopping`. The window uses `"window.dialogStyle": "custom"` so the prompt is visible in the recording.

### Before

![Before: after stopping, the System notification stays pending, and pressing Enter shows "You already have pending requests" instead of sending the message](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/blob/11e659c23f24593ca5dd660457080430d2706daf/20261015-171820-C23-F1/before.gif?raw=true)

### After

![After: the System notification is removed when the request stops, and the new message is sent and answered right away](https://github.com/karthiknadig/vscode/blob/11e659c23f24593ca5dd660457080430d2706daf/20261015-171820-C23-F1/after.gif?raw=true)

## How to test

1. Save `package.json` and `extension.js` from the first block below into a folder, for example `steering-repro/`.
2. Launch a dev build with it: `scripts\code.bat --extensionDevelopmentPath=<path>\steering-repro <empty folder>` (`./scripts/code.sh` on macOS/Linux). The test command is PowerShell, so on macOS/Linux replace `COMMAND` with an equivalent such as `sleep 5; for i in $(seq 12); do echo "line $i"; done`.
3. In the Chat view, check that **Repro Model** is selected in the model picker (the extension selects it at startup, or run **Steering Repro: Select Local Model**).
4. Send `@repro start` and click **Allow** for the terminal command. The response streams "Working, step N of 20".
5. About 5 seconds later, a "`Start-Sleep …` completed" System notification appears in the pending list while the response is still streaming. Press Alt+Backspace (or click Stop).
6. Type `@repro hello after stopping` and press Enter.
   - On `main`: the System notification is still pending, and Enter shows "You already have pending requests". Nothing is sent until you answer.
   - With this PR: the System notification disappears when you stop, and the message is sent right away. The participant replies "Received your message (…)".

```js
// Minimal chat participant used to reproduce steering + background terminal notifications.
// Plain JavaScript, no build step. Load it with --extensionDevelopmentPath.
const vscode = require('vscode');

const sleep = ms => new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

// Prints a few lines after a short delay, so the command finishes while the participant is still working.
const COMMAND = 'Start-Sleep -Seconds 5; 1..12 | ForEach-Object { "line $_" }';

// A local, offline language model so chat requests run without a Copilot sign-in.
// The participant below never calls it; it only has to be selectable.
const MODEL = { vendor: 'local-repro', id: 'repro-model', family: 'repro' };

function registerLocalModel(context) {
	context.subscriptions.push(vscode.lm.registerLanguageModelChatProvider(MODEL.vendor, {
		provideLanguageModelChatInformation() {
			return [{
				id: MODEL.id,
				name: 'Repro Model',
				family: MODEL.family,
				version: '1',
				maxInputTokens: 100000,
				maxOutputTokens: 4000,
				capabilities: { toolCalling: true },
				isUserSelectable: true,
			}];
		},
		async provideLanguageModelChatResponse(_model, _messages, _options, progress) {
			progress.report(new vscode.LanguageModelTextPart('ok'));
		},
		async provideTokenCount() {
			return 1;
		},
	}));
	const select = () => vscode.commands.executeCommand('workbench.action.chat.changeModel', MODEL).then(undefined, () => { });
	setTimeout(select, 1000);
	setTimeout(select, 4000);
	context.subscriptions.push(vscode.commands.registerCommand('steeringRepro.selectModel', select));
}

function activate(context) {
	registerLocalModel(context);
	const participant = vscode.chat.createChatParticipant('local.steeringRepro', async (request, chatContext, stream, token) => {
		if (request.isSystemInitiated) {
			stream.markdown(`Received a system notification (${request.prompt.length} characters).`);
			return {};
		}

		if (request.prompt.trim() === 'start') {
			stream.progress('Starting a background command');
			try {
				const result = await vscode.lm.invokeTool('run_in_terminal', {
					input: {
						command: COMMAND,
						explanation: 'Print a few lines after a short delay.',
						goal: 'Print lines in the background',
						mode: 'async',
					},
					toolInvocationToken: request.toolInvocationToken,
				}, token);
				const text = result.content.map(part => part.value ?? '').join('');
				stream.markdown(`Background command started (${text.length} characters of tool output).\n\n`);
			} catch (err) {
				stream.markdown(`Tool failed: ${err}\n\n`);
			}

			// Keep working for a while (ignoring yield requests) so the user can steer
			// and the background command can finish before this request ends.
			for (let i = 1; i <= 20 && !token.isCancellationRequested; i++) {
				stream.markdown(`Working, step ${i} of 20.\n\n`);
				await sleep(750);
			}
			return {};
		}

		stream.markdown(`Received your message (${request.prompt.length} characters).`);
		return {};
	});
	context.subscriptions.push(participant);
}

module.exports = { activate, deactivate() { } };

```

</details>

<details><summary>Automated repro scenario</summary>

Launch Code OSS as in step 2 with remote debugging enabled (`--remote-debugging-port=<port>`) and the user setting `"window.dialogStyle": "custom"`. Then run the scenario with a CDP scenario runner that passes `{ page, sleep, runCommand }` to each step (`page` is a Playwright page attached over CDP, and `runCommand` runs a Command Palette entry by title). Each step returns a string on success and throws on failure.

```js
// Repro: after the user stops a chat request while a background terminal notification is queued,
// the next message must be sent right away, and no stale "System notification" may stay pending.
// Harness: a CDP scenario runner against a Code OSS window launched with
//   --extensionDevelopmentPath=<folder with the @repro test extension>
// and "window.dialogStyle": "custom" so a confirmation dialog is rendered inside the window.
// The extension provides an offline model, so no Copilot sign-in is needed. The scenario approves the
// terminal command in chat when asked to.
const FOLLOW_UP = '@repro hello after stopping';

async function pasteIntoChat(page, text) {
	await page.evaluate(value => {
		const isVisible = element => !!element && element.getClientRects().length > 0;
		const editor = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.interactive-session .interactive-input-editor')).find(isVisible);
		if (!editor) {
			throw new Error('No visible chat input');
		}
		const target = editor.querySelector('.native-edit-context, textarea') ?? editor;
		target.focus();
		const data = new DataTransfer();
		data.setData('text/plain', value);
		target.dispatchEvent(new ClipboardEvent('paste', { clipboardData: data, bubbles: true, cancelable: true }));
	}, text);
	await page.waitForFunction(value => {
		const isVisible = element => !!element && element.getClientRects().length > 0;
		const editor = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.interactive-session .interactive-input-editor')).find(isVisible);
		const lines = Array.from(editor?.querySelectorAll('.view-line') ?? []).map(line => line.textContent ?? '').join('\n');
		return lines.replace(/\u00a0/g, ' ').includes(value);
	}, text, { timeout: 10000 });
}

/** Snapshot of the chat transcript rows in the visible chat view. */
function readTranscript(page) {
	return page.evaluate(() => {
		const isVisible = element => !!element && element.getClientRects().length > 0;
		const session = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.interactive-session')).find(isVisible);
		const rows = Array.from(session?.querySelectorAll('.interactive-list .monaco-list-row') ?? []);
		return rows.map(row => {
			const item = row.querySelector('.interactive-item-container');
			return {
				kind: item?.classList.contains('interactive-request') ? 'request' : item?.classList.contains('interactive-response') ? 'response' : 'other',
				pending: row.classList.contains('pending-request') || !!item?.classList.contains('pending-request') || !!row.querySelector('.pending-divider-label'),
				divider: row.querySelector('.pending-divider-label')?.textContent ?? undefined,
				system: !!item?.classList.contains('system-initiated-request') || !!row.querySelector('.system-initiated-request'),
				text: (item?.querySelector('.value')?.textContent ?? item?.textContent ?? '').replace(/\u00a0/g, ' ').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim(),
			};
		});
	});
}

/** Whether the visible chat view shows a running request (the input toolbar offers to stop it). */
function isRequestRunning(page) {
	return page.evaluate(() => {
		const isVisible = element => !!element && element.getClientRects().length > 0;
		const session = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.interactive-session')).find(isVisible);
		return Array.from(session?.querySelectorAll('.interactive-input-part .codicon-stop-circle, .interactive-input-part .codicon-debug-stop') ?? []).some(isVisible);
	});
}

/** Text of a visible dialog, if one is open. */
function readDialog(page) {
	return page.evaluate(() => {
		const dialog = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.monaco-dialog-box')).find(element => element.getClientRects().length > 0);
		return dialog ? (dialog.textContent ?? '').replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim() : undefined;
	});
}

/** Clicks the visible "Allow" button of a pending terminal confirmation in the transcript, if any. */
async function clickVisibleAllow(page) {
	const marked = await page.evaluate(() => {
		const buttons = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.interactive-session a.monaco-button'));
		const allow = buttons.filter(button => (button.textContent?.trim() ?? '') === 'Allow' && button.getClientRects().length > 0).at(-1);
		if (!allow) {
			return false;
		}
		allow.setAttribute('data-repro-allow', 'true');
		return true;
	});
	if (!marked) {
		return false;
	}
	await page.locator('[data-repro-allow="true"]').first().click();
	return true;
}

async function waitFor(check, timeout, description) {
	const deadline = Date.now() + timeout;
	let last;
	while (Date.now() < deadline) {
		last = await check();
		if (last?.ok) {
			return last;
		}
		await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 250));
	}
	throw new Error(`Timed out waiting for ${description}. ${last?.detail ?? ''}`.trim());
}

function waitForTranscript(page, predicate, timeout, description) {
	return waitFor(async () => {
		const rows = await readTranscript(page);
		return { ok: predicate(rows), rows, detail: `Transcript: ${JSON.stringify(rows).slice(0, 1500)}` };
	}, timeout, description).then(result => result.rows);
}

module.exports = {
	id: 'chat-send-after-stopping-with-queued-notification',
	title: 'Chat sends the next message after stopping a request that had a queued terminal notification',
	stepPauseMs: 900,
	steps: [
		{
			id: 'S1',
			title: 'Open a new chat in the Chat view',
			async run(ctx) {
				// Dismiss dialogs that block the window: one left open by an earlier run, or the
				// GitHub sign-in prompt of the throwaway profile (this scenario runs offline).
				const dismissDialogs = async () => {
					for (let i = 0; i < 4 && await readDialog(ctx.page); i++) {
						await ctx.page.keyboard.press('Escape');
						await ctx.sleep(700);
					}
				};
				await dismissDialogs();
				await ctx.runCommand('Notifications: Clear All Notifications');
				await ctx.runCommand('View: Close All Editors');
				await ctx.sleep(500);
				const newChat = ctx.page.locator('.part.auxiliarybar .action-label.codicon-plus[aria-label^="New Chat"]').first();
				if (!await newChat.isVisible().catch(() => false)) {
					await ctx.page.keyboard.press('Control+Alt+I');
				}
				await newChat.waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 15000 });
				await newChat.click();
				await ctx.page.locator('.part.auxiliarybar .interactive-session .interactive-input-editor').first().waitFor({ state: 'visible', timeout: 15000 });
				await waitForTranscript(ctx.page, rows => rows.length === 0, 10000, 'an empty chat');
				// Clear a draft left in the input by an earlier run.
				await ctx.page.locator('.part.auxiliarybar .interactive-session .interactive-input-editor').first().click();
				await ctx.page.keyboard.press('Control+A');
				await ctx.page.keyboard.press('Delete');
				// Pick the test extension's offline model (it registers shortly after startup).
				await ctx.runCommand('Steering Repro: Select Local Model');
				await ctx.sleep(1500);
				await dismissDialogs();
				await ctx.runCommand('Notifications: Clear All Notifications');
				return 'An empty chat is open in the Chat view';
			},
		},
		{
			id: 'S2',
			title: 'Ask @repro to start a background terminal command',
			async run(ctx) {
				await pasteIntoChat(ctx.page, '@repro start');
				await ctx.page.keyboard.press('Enter');
				// Approve the terminal command if the profile has not opted in to auto-approval yet.
				const deadline = Date.now() + 45000;
				let approved = false;
				while (Date.now() < deadline) {
					const rows = await readTranscript(ctx.page);
					if (rows.some(row => row.kind === 'response' && row.text.includes('Working, step 1'))) {
						break;
					}
					if (!approved && await clickVisibleAllow(ctx.page)) {
						approved = true;
					}
					await ctx.sleep(250);
				}
				await waitForTranscript(ctx.page, rows => rows.some(row => row.kind === 'response' && row.text.includes('Working, step 1')), 5000, 'the participant to start working');
				return `The background command started${approved ? ' (approved in chat)' : ''} and the participant keeps working`;
			},
		},
		{
			id: 'S3',
			title: 'The command finishes while the request runs; its notification is queued',
			async run(ctx) {
				await waitForTranscript(ctx.page, rows => rows.some(row => row.kind === 'request' && row.pending && row.system), 30000, 'the terminal completion notification to be pending');
				if (!await isRequestRunning(ctx.page)) {
					throw new Error('The request already ended before it could be stopped');
				}
				return 'A system notification is pending while the request is still running';
			},
		},
		{
			id: 'S4',
			title: 'Stop the request with Alt+Backspace',
			async run(ctx) {
				await ctx.page.locator('.part.auxiliarybar .interactive-session .interactive-input-editor').first().click();
				await ctx.page.keyboard.press('Alt+Backspace');
				await waitFor(async () => ({ ok: !await isRequestRunning(ctx.page) }), 10000, 'the request to stop');
				return 'The request stopped';
			},
		},
		{
			id: 'S5',
			title: `Send a new message: "${FOLLOW_UP}"`,
			async run(ctx) {
				await pasteIntoChat(ctx.page, FOLLOW_UP);
				await ctx.page.keyboard.press('Enter');
				await waitFor(async () => {
					const dialog = await readDialog(ctx.page);
					if (dialog) {
						return { ok: false, detail: `A dialog is shown instead: "${dialog}"` };
					}
					const rows = await readTranscript(ctx.page);
					const sent = rows.some(row => row.kind === 'request' && !row.pending && row.text.includes('hello after stopping'));
					const answered = rows.some(row => row.kind === 'response' && row.text.includes('Received your message'));
					return { ok: sent && answered, detail: `Transcript: ${JSON.stringify(rows).slice(0, 1500)}` };
				}, 15000, 'the new message to be sent and answered');
				return 'The message was sent right away and the participant answered it';
			},
		},
		{
			id: 'S6',
			title: 'No stale system notification is left in the queue',
			async run(ctx) {
				const rows = await readTranscript(ctx.page);
				const pending = rows.filter(row => row.pending && row.kind === 'request');
				if (pending.length) {
					throw new Error(`Still pending: ${JSON.stringify(pending).slice(0, 600)}`);
				}
				if (rows.some(row => row.kind === 'response' && row.text.includes('Received a system notification'))) {
					throw new Error('The stopped request\'s terminal notification was sent to the participant after the user stopped it');
				}
				return 'Nothing is pending and the stopped request\'s notification was not sent';
			},
		},
	],
};

```

</details>

## Validation

| Check | Command | Result |
|-------|---------|--------|

| Repro with this PR | same | ✅ passes 3 of 3 runs: the message is sent and answered, nothing is left pending, and the stopped request's notification is never sent |
| New unit tests without the fix (product code at `0861b77`) | `scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/chatService/chatService.test.ts --grep "system notifications queued while it ran"` | ❌ fails as expected: 1 failing (after a stop the notification was still pending and its send was never rejected), 1 passing ("send now" keeps it) |
| Chat service unit tests, including the existing steering, steering-merge and idle-notification tests | `scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/chatService/chatService.test.ts` | ✅ 283 passing |
| `run_in_terminal` unit tests | `scripts\test.bat --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/terminalContrib/chatAgentTools/test/electron-browser/runInTerminalTool.test.ts` | ✅ 224 passing, 107 pending (skipped on this platform), 0 failing |
| Typecheck | `npm run typecheck-client` | ✅ no errors |
| Lint | `npm run eslint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/common/chatService/chatServiceImpl.ts src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/test/common/chatService/chatService.test.ts` | ✅ no problems |
| Formatting | `node build/hygiene.ts <both files>` | ✅ passed |

Other behavior covered by the existing tests that still pass: steering while a request runs (the request is asked to yield and the steering message is sent next), a notification for a command that completes while no request is running is sent right away and keeps its provenance, and the earlier steering-batch rules (user messages and notifications are never merged into one request). This change does not touch the chat input, its keybindings or the queue and steer Enter bindings.

---
<sub>Found and fixed with automated exploratory testing. Draft until reviewed by a human.</sub>

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed loop, synchronous event chain, repeated full transcript/queue recomputation, and uncapped parallel notification source are all directly traced in repository code. Exact notification counts and device-specific frame impact vary, which limits severity rather than confidence in the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: main-thread queue scans, ChatRequestViewModel allocations, and chat list refreshes
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For K queued system notifications, each call scans/splices the remaining N-item queue and synchronously fires onDidChangePendingRequests; the visible widget then recomputes its transcript-wide T-item view and refreshes the list, making the stop path O(K*(N+T)) rather than one O(N+T) batch update.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Repeated synchronous list reconstruction and refresh can make the Stop action visibly stall or jank when several parallel background terminal completions have queued notifications in a long chat.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Canceling an active request did not mutate the pending queue, so it did not synchronously emit one pending-queue event and list refresh per queued system notification.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The added cancellation loop removes each matching notification through removePendingRequest separately, and each removal synchronously emits a pending-queue change before the next item is removed.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added lines 2682-2683 iterate every queued system notification and invoke removePendingRequest once per item; before this diff cancellation performed no queue removals or pending-queue UI notifications.
Findings.Title: Batch queued notification removals before refreshing the chat list
Findings.Impact: When an agent has launched several background terminals in parallel and their completion notifications accumulate while a long chat request is active, pressing Stop now performs and renders every intermediate queue state before returning to the user.
Findings.Evidence: runInTerminalTool.ts documents that background mode always creates a new terminal to allow parallel execution and maintains uncapped active-execution/background-notification maps. Each completion sends an isSystemInitiated steering request. ChatModel.removePendingRequest uses findIndex/splice and immediately fires onDidChangePendingRequests; ChatViewModel handles that event by invalidating its cache, ChatWidget calls onDidChangeItems, computeItems scans the full transcript and pending queue and creates pending ChatRequestViewModels, and onDidChangeItems refreshes the list. removePendingRequest also rescans the remaining queue for steering requests on every iteration.
Findings.Recommendation: Add a batched removal path that filters/replaces the pending queue once, emits one pending-queue change, completes each removed deferred, and resets yield state once; use it here so observers see only the final queue while preserving rejection semantics.

Scenarios.Scenario: User presses Stop on a local chat request while system-initiated terminal notifications are queued
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The Stop action awaits cancelCurrentRequestForSession. Existing cancellation is signaled first; the diff then synchronously scans the queue and removes every system notification before reaching the existing response-completion wait, so all queue events and visible chat-list refreshes are on the interaction's critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parallel background terminal commands produce one completion/input-needed notification per active terminal execution.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Up to one queued system notification per parallel background terminal completion; inspected maps and initialization path show no shared concurrency cap.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same terminal subprocesses and notifications existed, but Stop did not iterate and render each queued notification's removal.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The subprocesses run before/off the Stop cleanup critical path, but their accumulated notifications determine K and therefore the synchronous cleanup/rendering cost.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: CancellationTokenSource cancellation propagates to the active agent/tool invocation; the concrete provider may cross an extension-host or remote boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One active chat request plus its active tool calls per Stop action.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical cancellation propagation occurred before the PR, without per-notification queue removal work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This cancellation and the existing response-completion wait were already on the Stop path; the diff inserts local queue cleanup after signaling cancellation and before the wait.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: K system notifications among N pending requests and T transcript items. Background run_in_terminal explicitly creates separate terminals for parallel execution and has no shared cap in the inspected active-execution/notification maps, so multiple completions can accumulate; effective cardinality is K because there is no grouping or coalescing in the added loop.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Terminal commands can run in parallel, but cancellation cleanup is a serial loop. Every removal synchronously completes before the next and emits an observer update; no batching, limiter, or event coalescing protects the UI path.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: getPendingRequests returns the live array. ChatViewModel has a visible-items cache, but every removal event invalidates it before ChatWidget reads it, so the cache is cold K times; there is no queue-cleanup cache or coalescing. Positive/negative cache behavior is otherwise not relevant.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added per-item loop, serial queue scans, synchronous pending-request events, transcript recomputation, pending-view-model allocation, and list refresh are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The exact number of simultaneously completed background terminals and transcript size vary by workload and machine; this supports medium rather than high severity.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium rendering/latency regression: the PR adds K synchronous intermediate UI refreshes to the Stop critical path. Batch filtering, deferred rejection, yield reset, and a single queue event can preserve behavior.

Scenarios.Scenario: User chooses Send Now for a queued message in a local session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The target is reordered, the active request is canceled via cancelCurrentRequest(..., false), then processPendingRequests starts the selected queued request. The false flag skips the new notification-removal loop, preserving the previous critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Cancel the current agent/tool invocation and then invoke the selected pending request through the existing provider path.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cancellation followed by one selected request dispatch; queued notifications are processed later according to existing ordering.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The public cancellation method canceled the active request and processPendingRequests dispatched the selected request; the new private call with false preserves that behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Both cancellation and the next request dispatch are required for Send Now; the diff does not add or duplicate either boundary.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: N pending requests are already copied/mapped for reordering as before. The diff adds only a constant flag and private helper call; effective notification-removal cardinality is zero.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Cancellation remains serialized before starting the selected queued request. Queued system notifications remain ordered behind it; no changed burst or fan-out.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No new cache or invalidation behavior: the existing setPendingRequests event occurs once, and the new cancellation branch is not entered.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that no new scaling work or boundary is introduced on this branch.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider cancellation and request latency are implementation-dependent but unchanged by this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding: the false flag intentionally avoids the new cleanup and leaves boundary count, queue update count, and ordering unchanged.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cancel an active request in a server-managed/remote queue session
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Existing active-request cancellation remains critical. The added condition checks the session model and server-managed predicate, then short-circuits without scanning or mutating the pending queue.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Signal cancellation to the active server-managed agent session/provider.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One active request cancellation; no per-pending-message remote operation is introduced.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: One active-request cancellation with no local pending-message removal, matching the changed behavior for server-managed queues.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The existing cancellation boundary remains on the critical path. The new local condition short-circuits before any queue removal.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant local checks; effective queued-item cardinality is zero because server-managed sessions are excluded.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Remote queue ownership and cancellation behavior remain unchanged; no local loop, batching, or new concurrent operation occurs.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No local pending-queue cache is read or invalidated beyond obtaining the session model; remote queue synchronization behavior is unchanged.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the changed guard explicitly excludes server-managed queues before entering the loop.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Remote cancellation latency varies but is pre-existing and unaffected.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding: no changed remote fan-out or queue work occurs.

Scenarios.Scenario: Cancel is requested when no active request exists
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The existing early return and telemetry/logging path executes before all newly added queue-cleanup code.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Constant with respect to queued system notifications because the new branch is unreachable.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: No new scheduling or concurrency behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The existing pending-count read is unchanged; no added cache invalidation or queue mutation occurs.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: control flow returns before the added code.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding: behavior and cost are unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over both changed files and all diff pages. One introduced synchronous UI-work regression was reported for per-notification removal on local Stop; test-only additions and the Send Now, server-managed, and no-active-request branches introduce no reportable performance cost.
